title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In these 1986 notes Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic, essentially combinatorial theory of 'modèles de forme'. A set L carries a family S of 'intervals' satisfying axioms F1–F7, meant as models of (one-dimensional, tame) topological shapes. On the previous page he observed that a partial order on L can generate such a structure if it is (i) locally strictly filtering upward and downward ('loc. str. croissante et décroissante') and (ii) every element a has some a' < a < a''. Such an order defines a regular connected model of form satisfying F1–F5. He added that such an order need not be globally upward directed ('filtrant croissant'). This page supplies the counterexample.

(1) Crossed-out first attempt. Fix an irrational real r and let L = L1 ⊔ L2, with L1 = Q ∩ ]-∞, r] and L2 = (Q ∩ [r, +∞)) × E, where E is any set with card E ≥ 2.
- Since r is irrational, L1 has no maximum and Q ∩ [r, ∞) has no minimum.
- There are maps p : L → Q (surjective; the first coordinate) and q : L → E ⊔ {0}, with q = 0 on L1.
- The order is x < y iff p x < p y and some compatibility condition on q, presumably that q x = 0 or q x = q y.
- So L is a rational line which, above the Dedekind gap r, splits into card E branches. It is a 'Y-shaped' or branching line whose branch point is missing.
- He abandons the definition midway and generalizes.

(2) Retained example. Let L0 be an ordered set that is locally strictly filtering upward and downward, with every x admitting x' < x < x''. (The 'there exists x' is surely meant as 'for all x'.) Let (L_i), i ∈ I, be a family of ordered sets with the same properties. Put L = L0 ⊔ ∐_i L_i, ordered as follows:
- x < y if x, y lie in the same piece and x < y there;
- or if x ∈ L0 and y ∈ L_i for some i.

In modern terms this is the ordinal sum L0 ⊕ (∐_i L_i): L0 is placed below a disjoint union of the L_i, whose elements are mutually incomparable across different i.
- Locally nothing changes. Any x has strict lower and upper bounds, and order intervals around a point stay inside a single chain of pieces.
- So L satisfies the same local conditions, hence gives a model of form satisfying F1–F5.
- But two elements in different L_i have no common upper bound, so L is not upward directed.

Example (1) is the special case L0 = Q ∩ ]-∞, r[, L_e = Q ∩ ]r, ∞[ for e ∈ E. The point is that 'local filtering' does not globalize: these structures allow branching, as in trees or non-Hausdorff one-dimensional spaces. This motivates the next page's axiom F6, which works with 'branchements' (germs of branches at a boundary point x) and filtering only per branch.
errors: The written '∃ x ∈ L0, ∃ x' < a < a''' is a slip. The intended condition, as on the previous page, is '∀ x ∈ L0, ∃ x' < x < x''', and the letters x/a are mixed.
To get non-directedness one needs card I ≥ 2, with L0 and at least two L_i nonempty. This is unstated in example (2); it is stated as card E ≥ 2 in the crossed-out version.
The definition of the order in the crossed-out example is left unfinished (the condition on q is never written).

The phrase 'loc. str. croissante' is never precisely defined on this or the previous page, so the claim that L satisfies 'the same conditions' cannot be fully checked. Under the natural reading (order intervals around each point are filtering), it holds.

ideas.what: Counterexample: a line branching at an irrational Dedekind gap, Q below r and E copies of Q above r.
ideas.modern_name: branching line / non-Hausdorff 'Y' with a missing branch point; pretree with a gap
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical folklore (branching lines in non-Hausdorff 1-manifold theory)

ideas.what: Ordinal sum of a locally filtered poset with a disjoint union of such posets preserves the local conditions but destroys global upward directedness.
ideas.modern_name: ordinal (lexicographic) sum of posets; local vs global directedness

ideas.what: Using partial orders that are locally filtering, with no extremal points, to generate 'modèles de forme' (axioms F1–F5), as an approach to tame one-dimensional topology.
ideas.modern_name: order-theoretic models of 1-dimensional shapes; tame topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: programmatically Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme §5); o-minimality (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight) for tame topology
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of tame topology appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the axiomatics F1–F7 do not appear to be published.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatics of one-dimensional 'formes' via intervals and branchings anticipate or parallel the theory of pretrees, betweenness relations and dendrons (Ward, Bowditch, Adeleke–Neumann), and the order-theoretic study of non-Hausdorff 1-manifolds. This page's example is exactly the standard 'branching at a gap' in that theory. The link between his 'géométrie des formes' and pretree theory does not seem to have been made in the literature.
missed.quote: Elle satisfait les mêmes conditions que L0, Li mais n'est pas filtrant croissant!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly of historical interest: it situates the unpublished 'formes' axioms (F1–F7) relative to existing combinatorial theories of trees and branching. The example itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine counterexample (an ordinal sum, or a line branching at an irrational gap) showing that local filtering does not imply global directedness. Its interest lies only in the surrounding unpublished axiomatic project, not in this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 'q(x)=0 si x∈L': should read 'q(x)=0 si x∈L1'.
'Soit L0 un ordonné ... ni' is likely 'un ordonné muni [d'une relation]' or similar; 'filtrant' is crossed out twice.
'∃ x ∈ L0, ∃ x'<a<a''' in the image (letters x/a mixed), intended as ∀ x ∈ L0, ∃ x' < x < x''.
'une famille d'ens ordonnés, satisfaisant les mêmes conditions' is correct.
'On munit la relation d'ordre ... = l.o.' probably reads 'On munit L de la relation d'ordre'.
'ou bien x,y dans L0 et/ou Li': intended 'ou bien x, y dans un même Lα (α = 0 ou i ∈ I), et x < y dans Lα'.
